question_text: Calculate the displacement of the electrons or ions for the following conditions: (a) electronic polarization in nickel of $2 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^2$; (b) electronic polarization in aluminum of $2 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^2$ (c) ionic polarization in NaCl of $4.3 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^2$; and (d) ionic polarization in ZnS of $5 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^2$. Give your answer as a tuple: (displacement_nickel_m, displacement_NaCl_m).The units of each required answer are (m, m), respectively.
response:
For electronic polarization, the electron cloud of each atom (Z electrons) shifts by \(d\) relative to the nucleus, so \(P = NZe\,d\). For ionic polarization in NaCl, each ion pair carries charge \(e\), so \(P = ne\,d\).

- **Nickel** (FCC, \(a=0.352\) nm, \(Z=28\)): \(N=4/a^3\),  
  \(d = \dfrac{P}{ZeN} \approx 4.86\times10^{-19}\,\text{m}\)

- **NaCl** (rock salt, \(a=0.563\) nm, 4 formula units/cell): \(n=4/a^3\),  
  \(d = \dfrac{P}{en} \approx 1.20\times10^{-17}\,\text{m}\)

\[
\boxed{(4.86\times10^{-19},\ 1.20\times10^{-17})}
\]
